name: Shawwal
intro:
The month of Shawwal includes the passing of great figures and the occurrence of wars, just as several of the greatest enemies of the Ahl al-Bayt (PBUT) also met their doom in it. We will review days 1, 3, 4, 5, 6, 8, 14, 15, 17 and 25, which include these events. Eid al-Fitr is the first day of this month and the day of celebration of fasting.
The martyrdom of Imam Sadiq (PBUH) and Hazrat Hamza (PBUH), and the deaths of Aba Salt al-Harawi and Hazrat Abd al-Azim (PBUH), are days of sorrow in this month; to these calamities the destruction of the graves of the Imams of Baqi' (PBUT) has also been added. The death of Amr ibn al-As, the killing of Mutawakkil and the death of Abd al-Malik ibn Marwan are the sweetest days of this month, on which the enemies of the Ahl al-Bayt (PBUT) met their doom.
Among the war events of this month one can name the Battle of the Trench, Hunayn, Qarqarat al-Kudr, Hamra' al-Asad, Banu Qaynuqa', and the setting out for the Battle of Siffin, and the entry of Hazrat Muslim (PBUH) into Kufa is counted among the same kind. The return of the sun for Amir al-Mu'minin (PBUH) and the tawqi' (written decree) of Imam Zaman (PBUH) to Husayn ibn Ruh are other important events that occurred in this month.

events.title: Eid al-Fitr
events.text: The first of Shawwal is the day of Eid al-Fitr. Before the Eid prayer, it is recommended to pay the zakat al-fitra, wear fine clothes and visit Hazrat Sayyid al-Shuhada (PBUH).
sources: Masar al-Shi'a: p. 14. Tawdih al-Maqasid: p. 25.

events.title: The Death of Amr ibn al-As
events.text:
In the year 41 AH the vile Amr ibn al-As met his doom at the age of 90. His mother was Nabigha, a slave woman whom Abdullah ibn Jud'an bought and freed. She turned to immoral conduct, and because her price was cheaper than that of other women of ill repute, she had many clients. Thus she had ruined the reputation of Abdullah ibn Jud'an. Among them, in a single period of purity, Abu Lahab, Umayya ibn Khalaf, Hisham ibn al-Mughira, Abu Sufyan and al-As ibn Wa'il had illicit relations with her, and Amr ibn al-As came into being. When she gave birth, each of them claimed him. Finally they left the judgment to Nabigha herself, and she chose al-As. They said to her: Why did you choose al-As when the child resembles Abu Sufyan more? She said: Abu Sufyan is stingy and al-As provides better maintenance! This accursed al-As was the one who called the Prophet (SAWW) “abtar” (cut off, without posterity) and troubled the Hazrat's noble heart, until the blessed Surah al-Kawthar was revealed.
With this lineage and stock, it is no wonder that he was an enemy of the Prophet and of Ali ibn Abi Talib (PBUT), and that he and Mu'awiya filled the heart of Amir al-Mu'minin (PBUH) with blood throughout their lives. The Battle of Siffin, the raising of the Qur'an on spears, the martyrdom of Malik al-Ashtar, the affair of the arbitration, and the other deeds of that accursed one are well known.
At the time of his death he said: It is as if Mount Radwa has been placed on my neck and my insides are full of thorns, and I am being pulled out through the eye of a needle!
sources: Tatimmat al-Muntaha: p. 41. Masar al-Shi'a: p. 15. Qala'id al-Nuhur: vol. of Shawwal, p. 6. Fayd al-'Allam: pp. 61-62. Mustadrak Safinat al-Bihar: vol. 5, p. 213. Al-Ghadir: vol. 2, p. 175. Muruj al-Dhahab: vol. 3, p. 32.
Al-Ghadir: vol. 2, pp. 120-123.

events.title: The Battle of Qarqarat al-Kudr
events.text: On this day in the year 2 AH the Battle of Qarqarat al-Kudr took place. This name refers to a body of water belonging to the Banu Sulaym, three stages from Medina. The cause of this battle was that it had been reported to the Prophet (SAWW) that a group of the Banu Sulaym and Banu Ghatafan had gathered at Qarqarat al-Kudr to launch a night raid on Medina. So the Hazrat gave the banner of Islam to Amir al-Mu'minin (PBUH) and sent him there with two hundred men. When Amir al-Mu'minin (PBUH) arrived there, he saw that the group had fled from there, and as long as the Hazrat was there, no one returned.
sources: Mustadrak Safinat al-Bihar: vol. 5, p. 206.
Muntaha al-Amal: vol. 1, p. 58.

events.title: The Killing of Mutawakkil
events.text:
In the year 247 AH, on the night of Wednesday, the accursed Abbasid Mutawakkil was killed on the order of his son. His caliphate lasted 14 years and ten months and his ominous life 41 years.
Mutawakkil took the caliphate after Wathiq, in the year 232 AH. In his days there was a great deal of frivolity, sport and revelry, especially in his court. He was a man of vile character and, as Amir al-Mu'minin (PBUH) had said, the most disbelieving of the Abbasid family. He made Amr ibn Farj governor of Medina and Mecca, and he ordered the people that no one should show kindness to the family of Abi Talib, and that if anyone showed the slightest kindness he would be severely punished; things became so hard for the Alawids that the clothes of the Alawid women had become old and torn and they took turns wearing the one intact garment for prayer, and spun thread, until Mutawakkil met his doom.
Among the ugly and base deeds of Mutawakkil was that always and everywhere he spoke ill of Amir al-Mu'minin (PBUH) and was insolent toward him. He destroyed the blessed grave of Hazrat Sayyid al-Shuhada (PBUH) 17 times, but it was rebuilt again. Mutawakkil would cut off hands on the road to visit that Hazrat and kill the pilgrims.
Because of the insolence Mutawakkil showed toward Amir al-Mu'minin (PBUH) in a gathering, his son Muntasir, on the night of Wednesday, the third or fourth of Shawwal, commissioned several of his father's special slaves to kill him, and while Mutawakkil was drinking wine they fell upon him, and he rushed to the depths of hell.
On the same day that Mutawakkil was killed on the order of his son Muntasir, people pledged allegiance to Muntasir in the famous Ja'fari palace. Muntasir was outwardly a compassionate and kind man toward the Ahl al-Bayt of the Prophet (SAWW), and unlike his father he showed kindness to the family of Abi Talib and in no way harassed them.
He freed the visitation of Imam Husayn (PBUH) and did not obstruct anyone, ordered that Fadak be returned to the children of Imam Hasan and Imam Husayn (PBUT), freed the endowments (awqaf) of the family of Abi Talib (PBUT), and ordered that no one harass the Shi'a of Ali (PBUH). He also sent funds for the Alawid men and women of Medina to be distributed among them. He fell ill on 25 Rabi' al-Awwal in the year 248 and passed away in the afternoon of the fifth of Rabi' al-Thani, and the length of his caliphate was 6 months. It has been said that he was poisoned with a poison that had been put in the horn of a cupping instrument.
sources: Tawdih al-Maqasid: p. 26. Tatimmat al-Muntaha: p. 322. Bihar al-Anwar: vol. 50, p. 210. Fayd al-'Allam: p. 65. Tarikh Samarra': vol. 3, p. 324. Al-Bidaya wa al-Nihaya: vol. 10, p. 385. Tarikh Baghdad: vol. 2, p. 119.
Tatimmat al-Muntaha: pp. 330-332. Fayd al-'Allam: pp. 65, 66, 227. Tarikh al-Khulafa': p. 357.

events.title: The Battle of Hunayn
events.text: On this day in the year 8 AH, 15 days after the conquest of Mecca, the expedition of Hunayn took place. The Islamic army numbered 12,000 men, of whom 2,000 were from Mecca and 10,000 from Medina. In this battle four men were martyred, and the number of disbelievers killed has been written as more than 300. One of the instances of the flight of Abu Bakr and Umar was in this very battle. The date of this battle has also been reported as the month of Ramadan, and as 3, 10 and 11 Shawwal.
sources: Mustadrak Safinat al-Bihar: vol. 6, p. 65.
Tawdih al-Maqasid: p. 26. Bihar al-Anwar: vol. 21, p. 181. Al-Mawsu'a al-Kubra fi Ghazawat al-Nabi al-A'zam (SAWW): vol. 5, p. 6.
Fayd al-'Allam: p. 73.
Fayd al-'Allam: p. 67.

events.title: Setting Out for the Battle of Siffin
events.text: On such a day in the year 36 AH, Amir al-Mu'minin (PBUH) prepared to go to Siffin; and he appointed Abu Mas'ud Uqba ibn Amir al-Ansari as his deputy in Kufa.
sources: Tatimmat al-Muntaha: p. 23. Fayd al-'Allam: p. 69.

events.title: The Entry of Hazrat Muslim (PBUH) into Kufa
events.text: On such a day in the year 60 AH, Hazrat Muslim (PBUH) entered Kufa. The people of Kufa hurried to his service, listened to the letter of Imam Husayn (PBUH), and eighteen thousand people pledged allegiance to him. Muslim (PBUH) wrote a letter to Imam Husayn (PBUH) informing him of the pledge of the Kufans and asking him to come to Kufa.
sources: Qala'id al-Nuhur: vol. of Shawwal, p. 17. Farsan al-Hayja': vol. 2, p. 70. Fayd al-'Allam: p. 69. Sharh Ihqaq al-Haqq: vol. 32, p. 649. Waqa'i' al-Shuhur: p. 193.

events.title: The Tawqi' to Husayn ibn Ruh
events.text: On Sunday in the year 305 AH, the first tawqi' (written decree) of Imam Asr (PBUH) in the period of the Minor Occultation was issued to Husayn ibn Ruh (may God have mercy on him).
sources: Bihar al-Anwar: vol. 51, p. 356. Ghayba of Shaykh Tusi: p. 227. Waqa'i' al-Shuhur: p. 193.

events.title: The Destruction of the Graves of the Imams of Baqi' (PBUT)
events.text:
On this day in the year 1344 AH the graves of the Imams of Baqi' (PBUT), as well as the grave of Hazrat Hamza at Uhud, were destroyed by the Wahhabis.
The cause and motive for the destruction of these pure graves has been explained in various books written in refutation of the misguided beliefs of Wahhabism.
Besides the pure graves of the infallible Imams (PBUT), they also destroyed other graves, which are: the grave attributed to Fatima Zahra (PBUH), the pure grave of Fatima bint Asad (PBUH), mother of Amir al-Mu'minin (PBUH), the pure grave of Hazrat Umm al-Banin (PBUH), the grave of Ibrahim, son of the Prophet (SAWW), the grave of Isma'il, son of Hazrat Sadiq (PBUH), the graves of the daughters of the Prophet (SAWW), the grave of Halima Sa'diyya, the wet nurse of the Prophet (SAWW), and the graves of the martyrs of the time of the Prophet (SAWW).
In 1343 in Mecca the Wahhabis razed to the ground the domes over the graves of Hazrat Abd al-Muttalib, Abi Talib and Khadija, and the birthplaces of the Prophet (SAWW) and Fatima Zahra (PBUH). In Jeddah they also destroyed the grave of Eve and other graves.
In Medina they bombarded the Prophet's Mosque with cannon, but for fear of the Muslims they did not destroy the noble grave. In Shawwal 1344, by destroying the pure graves of the Imams of Baqi' (PBUT), they plundered the precious and valuable objects of those pure graves. They razed the grave of Hazrat Hamza (PBUH) and the martyrs of Uhud to the ground, and also demolished the dome and shrine of Hazrat Abdullah and Amina, the father and mother of the Prophet (SAWW), the grave of Isma'il son of Hazrat Sadiq (PBUH), and other graves.
In the same year they attacked Karbala al-Mu'alla, tore out the pure shrine and plundered the jewels and precious objects of the pure sanctuary, most of which were gifts of kings and very valuable and costly, and killed nearly 7,000 scholars, learned men, sayyids and ordinary people. Then they went toward Najaf, where they did not succeed in plundering and returned defeated.
sources: Mustadrak Safinat al-Bihar: vol. 6, pp. 65-66.
Kashf al-Irtiyab: p. 77. Shuhada' al-Fadila (Allama Amini): p. 388.

events.title: The Battle of Hamra' al-Asad
events.text:
On this day in the year 3 AH the Battle of Hamra' al-Asad took place. “Hamra' al-Asad” is the name of a place around Medina. After the Battle of Uhud and the Muslims' return to Medina, the Prophet (SAWW), lest the Quraysh return and attack Medina, ordered Bilal to make a call. It was the command of God Almighty that those who had been present at Uhud and had been wounded should pursue the enemy. The companions left off treating their wounds and put on their battle dress. Amir al-Mu'minin (PBUH) too, although he had received more than 80 wounds, some so deep that a wick (dressing) was placed inside them, put on battle dress, and the Messenger of God (SAWW), while looking at him and weeping, gave the banner to that Hazrat, and the Muslims set out.
After pursuing and charging the disbelievers, the Muslims stayed three days at Hamra' al-Asad and then returned to Medina.
sources: Mustadrak Safinat al-Bihar: vol. 6, pp. 65-66.
According to the view that places the Battle of Uhud on the seventh of Shawwal.
Bihar al-Anwar: vol. 20, pp. 1-146. Muntaha al-Amal: vol. 1, p. 64.

events.title: The Death of Abd al-Malik ibn Marwan
events.text:
In the year 86 AH the bloodthirsty, miserly Abd al-Malik ibn Marwan perished in Damascus, and some have mentioned 15 Shawwal. This was after he had usurped the caliphate for 21 years and 6 months. Before his reign he constantly frequented the mosque and recited the Qur'an, and he was called “Hamamat al-Masjid” (the dove of the mosque)! When the news of sovereignty reached him, he closed the Qur'an and said: “Salamun alayka, hadha firaqun bayni wa baynik” (Peace be upon you; this is the parting between me and you); “Farewell, this is the beginning of separation between you and me”!!
When his illness became severe, the doctor said: If he drinks water he will die. But thirst overcame him and he asked his son Walid for water. He said: If you drink water you will die! Abd al-Malik pleaded with his daughter to give him water, but his son Walid prevented it. Abd al-Malik said: Let them give me water, or I will remove you from the crown princeship; Walid allowed it, and Abd al-Malik drank water and died.
Among his greatest crimes were the martyrdom of Imam Zayn al-Abidin (PBUH) and setting Hajjaj al-Thaqafi over the Shi'a of Amir al-Mu'minin (PBUH).
sources: Tatimmat al-Muntaha: p. 105. Fayd al-'Allam: p. 73. Mustadrak Safinat al-Bihar: vol. 5, p. 216.
Qala'id al-Nuhur: vol. of Shawwal, p. 94.
Muntaha al-Amal: vol. 2, p. 39. Tatimmat al-Muntaha: p. 106.

events.title: The Battle of Uhud and the Martyrdom of Hazrat Hamza (PBUH)
events.text: In the year 3 AH, on the day of the Battle of Uhud, Hazrat Hamza, Sayyid al-Shuhada, and 69 of the Muslims were martyred. In this battle the Muslims numbered one thousand, of whom, according to some writers, three hundred turned back on the way, and 700 remained for the fighting. The disbelievers numbered 3000; 2000, 4000 and 5000 have also been said. The number of disbelievers killed was 22 or 23 or 28, and the number of martyrs was 70. On this day the Prophet's (SAWW) tooth was broken and his forehead injured.
sources: Masar al-Shi'a: pp. 15-17. Bihar al-Anwar: vol. 20, p. 18. Tawdih al-Maqasid: p. 27. Sirat Ibn Hisham: vol. 3, p. 68. Al-Mawsu'a al-Kubra fi Ghazawat al-Nabi al-A'zam (SAWW): vol. 2, p. 110. Taqwim al-Muhsinin: p. 12.
Masar al-Shi'a: p. 15.
Bihar al-Anwar: vol. 20, p. 18.

subsections.title: The Self-Sacrifice of Amir al-Mu'minin (PBUH) at Uhud
subsections.text:
On this day, as a result of the self-sacrifice and courage that Amir al-Mu'minin (PBUH) showed in defending the noble person of the Seal of the Prophets (SAWW) and protecting him, many wounds were inflicted on his blessed body. This was while others had fled, and the Prophet (SAWW) said: O Ali, do you hear that they are praising you from the heavens? One of the angels, named Ridwan, says: “La sayfa illa Dhulfiqar wa la fata illa Ali” (There is no sword but Dhulfiqar and no young hero but Ali). Amir al-Mu'minin (PBUH) says: I wept for joy and praised God, the Glorified, for this blessing.
In this battle victory was at first with the Muslims, but after they went some distance in pursuit of the enemy and the field was emptied, they returned and busied themselves with collecting booty, and most of the guards disobeyed the order of the Prophet (SAWW), left their guard posts and, like the rest, busied themselves with collecting booty.
Khalid ibn Walid, who was one of the leaders of the disbelievers in this battle, attacked with the disbelievers from that very section. The small number of guards of the pass who had not left were martyred, and the disbelievers attacked the Muslims from behind. The fleeing disbelievers, when they saw this situation, returned as well, and the attack on the Muslims intensified. Many wounds were inflicted on the blessed body of the Prophet (SAWW), and Satan cried out that Muhammad has been killed! The Muslims, hearing this cry, fled, and only a few people were protecting the blessed person of the Prophet (SAWW), namely Amir al-Mu'minin (PBUH), Abu Dujana, who was martyred, a woman named Nusayba, and Anas ibn al-Nadr, who had just arrived from Medina.
sources: Irshad: vol. 1, p. 87. Usd al-Ghaba: vol. 4, p. 21. Masar al-Shi'a: p. 16. Misbah of Kaf'ami: vol. 2, p. 600.

subsections.title: Abu Bakr and Umar in the Battle of Uhud
subsections.text:
Umar ibn al-Khattab says: At Uhud we had pledged allegiance to the Prophet (SAWW) that no one would flee, and whoever among us fled would be astray and misguided, and whoever among us was killed would be a martyr.
Ahmad ibn Hanbal says: Abu Bakr and Umar fled in this battle. When Amir al-Mu'minin (PBUH) was pursuing the fugitives, Umar, wiping tears from his eyes, returned and said to Amir al-Mu'minin (PBUH): Forgive me!! Amir al-Mu'minin (PBUH) said: “Was it not you who shouted: Muhammad has been killed, return to your former religion?!!” Umar said: It was Abu Bakr who said this! It was here that this verse was revealed: “Inna alladhina tawallaw minkum yawma iltaqa al-jam'ani innama istazallahumu al-shaytan” (Those of you who turned back on the day the two armies met - it was only Satan who caused them to slip).
Imam Sadiq (PBUH) says: In the Battle of Uhud Amir al-Mu'minin (PBUH) was defending the Prophet (SAWW), while the other companions were fleeing. That Hazrat, like an angry lion, went after the fugitives and first reached Umar ibn al-Khattab, who, together with Uthman, Harith ibn Hatib and a number of others, was fleeing rapidly. The Hazrat cried out: O group, you broke the pledge and left the Prophet (SAWW) alone and are fleeing toward hell?
Umar ibn al-Khattab says: I saw Ali with a broad sword from which death dripped, and his eyes in anger gleamed like two cups of blood, or like two bowls of oil in which a fire had been lit, and I understood that if he reached us he would kill us in a single charge. So I went forward and said: “Ya Aba al-Hasan, I adjure you by God to leave us alone, for it is the custom of the Arabs that sometimes they flee and sometimes they attack, and when they attack they make up for their fleeing.” So that Hazrat left us; and by God, such a fear of that Hazrat fell into my heart that to this day it has not left my heart.
In this battle, while protecting the Prophet (SAWW), 90 wounds were inflicted on the blessed body of Amir al-Mu'minin (PBUH), on his blessed face, head, chest, belly, hands and feet. Gabriel descended and said: “O Muhammad, by God, this act of Ali ibn Abi Talib is true solidarity (muwasat).” The Prophet (SAWW) said: “That is because I am from him and he is from me.” Gabriel said: “And I am from the two of you.”
sources: Bihar al-Anwar: vol. 20, pp. 53-54.
Surah Al Imran: verse 155. Ithbat al-Hudat: vol. 2, pp. 364-365.
Bihar al-Anwar: vol. 20, pp. 53-54. Qala'id al-Nuhur: vol. of Shawwal, p. 77.
Bihar al-Anwar: vol. 20, p. 54.

subsections.title: A Woman Named Nusayba at the Battle of Uhud
subsections.text: On this day one of those who sacrificed herself and did not flee, but also prevented others from fleeing, was a woman named Nusayba, daughter of Ka'b ibn Maziniyya, who was called Umm Umara. She took part in the Battle of Uhud with her husband and two sons. Nusayba carried a waterskin on her shoulder and was watering the army of Islam. When she saw the situation, that the Muslims were fleeing, she threw the waterskin aside and made herself a shield before the Prophet (SAWW), such that many wounds were inflicted on her, the treatment of one of which continued for a year afterward. This devoted woman took up a sword and struck such a blow at Ibn Hamiyya, who intended to kill the Prophet (SAWW), that he fled. Her son Abdullah wanted to flee, but she prevented him and encouraged him to fight and defend the Prophet (SAWW), and he accepted. The Prophet (SAWW) said to Nusayba: “Barak Allahu alayki, ya Nusayba” (God bless you, O Nusayba). At this point the Prophet (SAWW) saw one of the Muhajirun fleeing with his shield tied to his back. The Hazrat said: “O bearer of the shield, throw down your shield and go to hell.” Then the Hazrat said to Nusayba: “Take his shield.” She took it and began fighting the polytheists. At this the Hazrat said: “The station of Nusayba is superior to the station of so-and-so and so-and-so, because they fled.”
sources: Bihar al-Anwar: vol. 20, p. 54.

subsections.title: The Martyrdom of Hazrat Hamza (PBUH)
subsections.text:
On this day Hamza ibn Abd al-Muttalib (PBUH) was martyred.
That Hazrat was the milk brother of the Prophet (SAWW), because both noble ones had been nursed by a woman named Thuwayba.
That Hazrat was a brave and imposing man, and in this battle he was killed by Wahshi on the order of Hind, wife of Abu Sufyan. Hind, because of the killing of her father, brother and uncle at the Battle of Badr, at first intended to dig up the grave of the mother of the Prophet (SAWW), but the Quraysh disbelievers, fearing the exhumation of their own dead, prevented her. So she incited Wahshi with promises to kill the Prophet (SAWW) or Ali al-Murtada (PBUH) or Hamza. Wahshi said: “I am unable to kill the Prophet (SAWW) and his cousin Ali (PBUH), but I will lie in wait to kill Hamza.” In the battlefield he struck that Hazrat on his blessed chest or belly with a spear and martyred him. When they gave the news to Hind, that vile woman ordered that his chest be split open and his blessed liver be taken out. When she tried to bite into Hamza's liver, her ominous teeth were of no avail. Hind also cut off that Hazrat's ears, nose, etc. with a dagger and hung them around her neck.
When the Prophet (SAWW) saw Hamza in that state, he wept and drew his blessed cloak over him so that his sister Safiyya would not see him in that condition, and said: “Ya amma Rasul Allah wa Asad Allah wa Asad Rasulihi... ya fa'il al-khayrat, kashif al-kurubat....” (O uncle of the Messenger of God, lion of God and lion of His Messenger... O doer of good deeds, remover of distresses....) Amir al-Mu'minin and Fatima Zahra (PBUH), Safiyya and others wept for that Hazrat. The Prophet (SAWW) prayed over his blessed body, and they buried him at Uhud. After forty years, when Mu'awiya wanted to run a canal through Uhud, he came upon the grave of Hazrat Hamza, and the tip of the shovels reached Hamza's foot and blood immediately flowed!
Hazrat Reza (PBUH), quoting the Messenger of God (SAWW), said: “The best of my brothers is Ali (PBUH) and the best of my uncles is Hamza.”
sources: Bihar al-Anwar: vol. 15, p. 281.
Bihar al-Anwar: vol. 20, p. 55. Hamza Sayyid al-Shuhada (PBUH): pp. 28-29.
Uyun Akhbar al-Reza (PBUH): vol. 2, p. 61. Riyahin al-Shari'a: vol. 4, p. 350.

events.title: The Return of the Sun (Radd al-Shams)
events.text:
On this day the return of the sun for Amir al-Mu'minin (PBUH) took place. According to one view, this event was on 17 Shawwal.
It should be noted that the return of the sun for Amir al-Mu'minin (PBUH) occurred twice: once in the time of the Prophet (SAWW) near the Quba Mosque, and the other after the passing of that Hazrat in the land of Babylon near Hillah.
Allama Amini (may God have mercy on him) has described in detail in al-Ghadir the hadiths of the return of the sun through various chains, as well as those who have written books about the return of the sun.
sources: Qala'id al-Nuhur: vol. of Shawwal, p. 92. Misbah of Kaf'ami: vol. 2, p. 600. Fayd al-'Allam: p. 76. Taqwim al-Muhsinin: p. 12. Waqa'i' al-Shuhur: p. 201.
Bihar al-Anwar: vol. 97, p. 384; vol. 95, p. 189.
Fayd al-'Allam: p. 201.
Al-Ghadir: vol. 3, pp. 183-204.

events.title: The Battle of Banu Qaynuqa'
events.text: On this day, twenty months after the Prophet's Hijra, the expedition of Banu Qaynuqa' took place; according to one view, this battle took place in Safar.
sources: Bihar al-Anwar: vol. 20, p. 5.

events.title: The Death of Hazrat Abd al-Azim (PBUH)
events.text:
In the year 252 or 255 AH Hazrat Abu al-Qasim Abd al-Azim al-Hasani, son of Abdullah ibn Ali ibn Hasan ibn Zayd ibn Hasan ibn Ali ibn Abi Talib (PBUT), passed away. He was among the famous scholars and among the trustworthy and distinguished hadith transmitters, was proverbial among elite and common alike for asceticism and piety, and transmitted narrations from Imam Jawad and Imam Hadi (PBUT). The Book of the Sermons of Amir al-Mu'minin (PBUH) and Kitab al-Yawm wa al-Layla are among that noble man's works. The eminence and greatness of his stature is clear from his presenting his beliefs to his Imam of the time, Hazrat Hadi (PBUH), and that Hazrat's confirmation of them.
He entered Rayy incognito and, for fear of the Abbasids, lived in the house of one of the Shi'a in the Sarbanan (camel-drivers') quarter. No one realized who that noble man was until his death, when, wanting to wash his body after he died, they found a note in his clothing in which he had written his noble lineage. His pure shrine in the city of Rayy is famous.
That Hazrat's father Abdullah is known as “Abdullah Qafa.” “Qafa” was the name of a place of which Abdullah was governor on behalf of his grandfather Hasan ibn Zayd.
The wife of Hazrat Abd al-Azim is Khadija, daughter of Qasim ibn Hasan ibn Zayd ibn Hasan ibn Ali ibn Abi Talib (PBUT). Some consider Imamzadeh Qasim of northern Tehran to be the father of Khadija, wife of Hazrat Abd al-Azim.
His daughter is Salma, whom Hazrat Abd al-Azim (PBUH) gave in marriage to Muhammad ibn Ibrahim ibn Ibrahim ibn Hasan ibn Zayd ibn Hasan ibn Ali ibn Abi Talib (PBUT), and the fruit of this marriage was three sons named Abdullah, Hasan and Ahmad.

events.title: The Battle of the Trench (Khandaq)
events.text:
On this day in the year 5 AH the expedition of the Trench (Ahzab) and the killing of Amr ibn Abdwud at the hands of Amir al-Mu'minin (PBUH) took place, and this battle occurred in winter. Some have placed the Battle of the Trench on 8 Dhu al-Qa'da and some on 15 Shawwal, and it is not implausible that the battle began on 15 Shawwal. Also, according to one view, the expedition of the Trench occurred in 4 AH. In this battle the number of Muslims was 3000 and the number of Muslim martyrs was 6. The number of disbelievers was 10000, but the number of disbelievers killed has not been stated.
In this battle the Muslims dug a trench around the city, inside Medina. While this work was under way the hypocrites showed insolence toward the Prophet (SAWW), and Amr ibn Abdwud called for a duelist, but no one dared. Umar ibn al-Khattab spoke of Amr's feats of bravery and instilled fear in the people.
Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf said: “If Amr overpowers us he will kill all of us. The best way is to hand Muhammad over to them bound”!! In such circumstances the Prophet (SAWW) said: Is there a friend who will suffice against the evil of this enemy? Our master and lord, the Lion of God, the Victorious, Ali ibn Abi Talib (PBUH) said: I will go to fight him. The Prophet (SAWW) was silent, and said these words up to three times, and all three times Amir al-Mu'minin (PBUH) declared his readiness to fight.
Finally the Prophet (SAWW) gave permission and Amir al-Mu'minin (PBUH) set out. At this the Prophet (SAWW) said: “Barraza al-iman kulluhu ila al-shirk kullih” (The whole of faith has come forth against the whole of polytheism).
After Amr ibn Abdwud did not accept Islam and did not give up fighting, Amir al-Mu'minin (PBUH) brought him down with a single blow. At this the Muslims' cries of takbir rose and the Prophet (SAWW) said: The duel of Ali ibn Abi Talib (PBUH) on the day of the Trench is superior to the deeds of my nation until the Day of Resurrection.
sources: Fayd al-'Allam: pp. 76-77. Qala'id al-Nuhur: vol. of Shawwal, p. 107.

events.title: The Death of Aba Salt al-Harawi
events.text:
On this day in the year 207 AH the eminent trustworthy Aba Salt Abd al-Salam ibn Salih al-Harawi, who was from Herat, passed away after his release from Ma'mun's prison.
Aba Salt was among the companions of Imam Reza (PBUH) and among the elite of the Shi'a, and the book “Wafat al-Reza (PBUH)” (The Death of Reza) is his work. In Iran two graves are attributed to that noble man: one outside the city of Mashhad, and the other at the Rayy Gate of Qom.
sources: Mustadrak Safinat al-Bihar: vol. 5, p. 224.
Maraqid al-Ma'arif: vol. 1, pp. 107-108.

events.title: The Arrest of Imam Kazim (PBUH)
events.text: On this day the accursed Harun came to the Mosque of the Prophet (SAWW), outwardly to visit it but in truth to arrest Hazrat Musa ibn Ja'far (PBUH), and sent that Hazrat from Medina to Baghdad.
sources: Kafi: vol. 2, p. 507. Bihar al-Anwar: vol. 48, p. 206.

events.title: The Martyrdom of Imam Sadiq (PBUH)
events.text:
Imam Sadiq (PBUH) passed away on such a day in the year 148 AH. The middle of Rajab and the middle of Shawwal have also been given for the Hazrat's martyrdom.
The Hazrat's martyrdom was due to poisoned grapes that Mansur fed him. The length of his imamate was 34 years and his noble age was 65 years.
The era of that Hazrat's imamate coincided with seven usurping rulers, who are: Hisham ibn Abd al-Malik, Walid ibn Yazid ibn Abd al-Malik, Yazid ibn Walid, Ibrahim ibn Walid and Marwan al-Himar of the Banu Umayya, and Saffah and Mansur Dawaniqi of the Banu Abbas.
The children of that Hazrat are seven sons and three daughters: Hazrat Musa ibn Ja'far (PBUH), Isma'il, Abdullah, Muhammad Dibaj, Ishaq, Ali Uraydi (Ali ibn Ja'far, buried in Qom), Abbas, Umm Farwa, Asma and Fatima.
sources: Qala'id al-Nuhur: vol. of Shawwal, p. 139. A'lam al-Wara: vol. 1, p. 514. Jannat al-Khulud: p. 27. Mustadrak Safinat al-Bihar: vol. 6, p. 66. Kafi: vol. 2, p. 377. Irshad: vol. 2, p. 180.
